entries.name: Open and drain the clay
entries.when_to_act: Before the first heavy rain, while the ground is still workable.
entries.how_to_tell_ready: A spade cuts in about a hand's depth and the ground holds loose clods instead of bouncing back.
entries.why_it_matters: Salt only washes out through soil that is open and drains. Hard packed clay lets rain run off and leaves the salt where it is.

entries.name: Flush the salt down
entries.when_to_act: After the first heavy rain, and again after each heavy rain while the white crust keeps returning.
entries.how_to_tell_ready: The water leaving through the low end runs clear, and the surface no longer dries white.
entries.why_it_matters: Salt leaves with water. Flushing works only while the soil is open and the water has somewhere to go.

entries.name: Sow the grasses
entries.when_to_act: When the soil crumbles in your hand and the crust has eased after flushing.
entries.how_to_tell_ready: A damp handful crumbles into soft lumps instead of rolling into a slick ribbon.
entries.why_it_matters: Seed on hard salty ground dries out and dies. Seed on crumbled ground takes root and starts holding the soil.

entries.name: Sow the warm season grain
entries.when_to_act: When the ground has warmed after the first heavy rain and the soil crumbles.
entries.how_to_tell_ready: The soil feels warm to your bare palm, crumbles dry in your fist, and no water stands in the dips.
entries.why_it_matters: Warm, open, crumbled ground lets young roots push down to water before the heat sets in.

entries.name: Sow the rice
entries.when_to_act: When the mud holds a shallow layer of water and the worst of the salt has flushed out.
entries.how_to_tell_ready: Water sits a hand's depth deep in the walled plot, runs cloudy rather than oily, and the crust stays away.
entries.why_it_matters: Rice needs standing water to grow, and the same water keeps washing salt down and out of the clay.

entries.name: Sow the cool season crops
entries.when_to_act: As the heavy rains ease and the ground starts to dry and crumble.
entries.how_to_tell_ready: The puddles have gone, the ground crumbles dry underfoot, and a spade lifts it without sticking.
entries.why_it_matters: These crops like a drier finish. Sown too early into wet clay they rot; sown too late they dry out before they fill.

entries.name: Dig the green manure in
entries.when_to_act: Before the plants flower and set seed, while they are still green.
entries.how_to_tell_ready: The plants stand about knee to waist high with flowers just opening.
entries.why_it_matters: Green plants dug into the soil feed it and help salt wash out. Once they seed, the plot has to be cleared instead of fed.

entries.name: Cut the green fodder
entries.when_to_act: When the grass reaches your knee, and again each time it recovers.
entries.how_to_tell_ready: Fresh shoots are rising again from the base of the cut clumps.
entries.why_it_matters: Cutting at the right height keeps the grass thick and spreading, so it covers and heals the ground while it feeds animals.

entries.name: Plant the trees
entries.when_to_act: At the start of the rains, or the start of the warm season for the palm.
entries.how_to_tell_ready: The ground is soaked through deep after rain and soft to a spade, and water can be carried to the planting spot.
entries.why_it_matters: A young tree set into soaked, fed ground roots before the dry spell arrives and has the strength to live on salty ground.

entries.name: Harvest the grain
entries.when_to_act: When the heads droop, turn brown and dry, and rattle in the wind.
entries.how_to_tell_ready: A head rubbed between your palms lets the grain rub clean off the stalk.
entries.why_it_matters: Cut too soon the grain will not keep; left too long the wind and birds take it.

entries.name: Harvest the root and oil crops
entries.when_to_act: When the leaves yellow and flop over, or when the seed pods rattle.
entries.how_to_tell_ready: Pods crackle and split when pressed between your fingers; roots lift clean out of ground you have loosened.
entries.why_it_matters: Lifting at the right time saves the crop. Roots pulled too early are small and will not store; pods left too long shatter on the stalk.

entries.name: Keep watching for the crust
entries.when_to_act: One moon after flushing, and again after each long dry spell.
entries.how_to_tell_ready: The white crust stays away and the crumbs on the surface still feel soft under your fingers.
entries.why_it_matters: Salt comes back up as the ground dries. Catching it early keeps the work of flushing, rather than letting the land harden again.
